title: Feeding Our Future Ringleader Sentenced to 500 Months

supports: Aimee Bock, 44, founder and executive director of Feeding Our Future, was sentenced on May 22, 2026 to 500 months in prison for her lead role in the Feeding Our Future fraud scheme, announced U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen.
Salim Said, 36, former co-owner of Safari Restaurant, was jointly tried with Bock.
Feeding Our Future received more than $18 million in administrative fees to which it was not entitled, per the release.

The release states Feeding Our Future opened more than 250 Federal Child Nutrition Program sites, going from about $3.4 million in disbursed federal funds in 2019 to nearly $200 million in 2021, and fraudulently obtained and disbursed more than $240 million in Federal Child Nutrition Program funds overall.

U.S. District Judge Nancy Brasel is quoted at sentencing: 'This was a fraud vortex and you were at the epicenter of it,' and 'A sentence of less than 500 months would not do justice to the people of Minnesota.'
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald is quoted characterizing the sentence as 'over 41 years in prison.'
does_not_support: A restitution or forfeiture dollar figure specific to Bock's sentencing; none is stated in the retrieved text of this release.
